title: Partition hot control_events table by tenant range and introduce materialized views for dashboard read paths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Context: The control_events table is a top-5 hotspot in the control plane: heavy write churn from tenant activity plus wide scans from the Console dashboard. This ticket proposes splitting the monolithic table into tenant_range partitions (hash-range on tenant_id) and creating read-optimized materialized views for dashboard queries to drastically reduce tail latency on API listing pages and lower scan amplification. Goal: reduce 95th-percentile dashboard read latency by 60% and reduce nightly compaction I/O by 30%.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane dashboard listing queries 95p latency reduced >= 60% in staging compared to baseline (measured over 48h load tests)
New partitions added with online migrations; no more than 1 minute of disruption for control-plane writes during cutover
Materialized views refresh strategy implemented (incremental refresh using WAL/CDC) and shows <= 5s eventual consistency for dashboard reads
Automated rollback available and exercised in a dry run
DB storage growth rate for control_events reduced or unchanged vs baseline after compaction settings tuned
migration_steps: Create tenant_range partitioned table control_events_shard (same schema) using tenant_id range buckets (initially 128 ranges)
Deploy application-layer multi-write: write to control_events (legacy) AND control_events_shard for 24h in staging
Run background verifier job comparing row counts and checksums by tenant between legacy and shard tables
Stream-copy historical data in tenant-ordered batches using CDC-based backfill; prioritize top 500 tenants by activity
Switch reads for dashboard route to materialized view on control_events_shard during low-traffic window
Monitor for 48h, then flip writes to only shard table and deprecate legacy table
rollback_plan: If errors or unacceptable latency observed during staged cutover: revert API reads to legacy control_events table, re-enable multi-write to legacy+shard, pause refreshers for materialized views, and open rollback incident channel. Keep a snapshot of new partitions for forensic analysis. Expected rollback time: <30 minutes for reads, <2 hours to re-enable writes under multi-write path.
db_impact: Estimate: ~1.6TB additional temporary storage during full backfill across shards. Expected long-term storage +/-5% after compaction. Write amplification reduced for most dashboard queries due to smaller per-partition index sizes.
measurements: Backfill throughput target: 40k rows/sec to avoid replication spikes
Max acceptable replication lag during migration: 30s
notes: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting — agreed on 128 initial ranges; Diego to prototype range mapping script.
2026-02-20: Decision: use tenant_id range buckets (stable across rebalances) instead of pure hash to allow tenant affinity for multi-region later.
2026-02-25: Prototype backfill in staging completed; observed write amplification spike when parallelism > 12. Throttled backfill to 8 workers.
2026-02-28: Security review flagged KMS key usage for CDC snapshots. Raised security_review_required flag and engaged security team.
2026-03-01: Running 24h multi-write in staging; verifier job shows 99.998% checksum parity for top-200 tenants.
Open questions: optimal partition count at 10k tenants; we may add auto-split logic post-cutover.
